notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (product docs + support) focused on switching from Pinecone-hosted POC to Redwood hosted -> Dedicated. Product team is pragmatic: want lowest total cost + predictable latency. Key ask is a repeatable POC that demonstrates (1) embeddings throughput for nightly batches, (2) low-latency search at 150-250 QPS, (3) simple integration to pgvector in our AWS Postgres cluster.

POC details / callouts:
- POC ran on Redwood hosted API for 2 weeks against 500k doc sample. Relevance improved ~12% on our eval set vs baseline (internal eval), but noticed bulk upsert throttling during ingest windows.
- Team quote: "If nightly embedding jobs take >2x our current window, product team blocks go-live."
- Cost sensitivity: current Pinecone + OpenAI embedding stack ~ $6k/mo for this slice; Lumina Harbor expects Redwood to be competitive at scale or show clear ops benefits for Dedicated.
- Integration: devs prefer to use Postgres + pgvector. Need documented best-practice for streaming upserts (small batches) vs bulk upserts. Also want samples for batch retry/backoff patterns.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration; legal will require data residency statements for EU customers (we have EU customers).
- SLA: procurement pushing for 99.9% uptime in contract; AE to confirm Dedicated SLA options and remedies.

Open questions / blockers:
- Redwood recommended Dedicated sizing for 6-month reserved pool; need granular per-token + per-embedding cost comparison vs our Pinecone line item. (blocker: pricing clarity)
- pgvector performance with Redwood host pipeline vs doing embeddings in Redwood + persisting vectors to our Postgres - engineering wants benchmark numbers for throughput and end-to-end latency.
- Legal/Privacy: need sample DPA and info on data-at-rest residency.
